name: Governance
definition: Governance includes oversight, strategies, policies, and IT asset management to implement an effective governance of the cybersecurity program.

name: Risk Management
definition: Risk Management includes a risk management program, risk assessment process, and audit function to effectively manage risk and assess the effectiveness of key controls.

name: Resources
definition: Resources include staffing, tools, and budgeting processes to ensure the institution’s staff or external resources have knowledge and experience commensurate with the institution’s risk profile.

name: Training and Culture
definition: Training and Culture includes the employee training and customer awareness programs contributing to an organizational culture that emphasizes the mitigation of cybersecurity threats.

name: Threat Intelligence
definition: Threat Intelligence refers to the acquisition and analysis of information to identify, track, and predict cyber capabilities, intentions, and activities that offer courses of action to enhance decision making.

name: Monitoring and Analyzing
definition: Monitoring and Analyzing refers to how an institution monitors threat sources and what analysis may be performed to identify threats that are specific to the institution or to resolve conflicts in the different threat intelligence streams.

name: Information Sharing
definition: Information Sharing encompasses establishing relationships with peers and information-sharing forums and how threat information is communicated to those groups as well as internal stakeholders.

name: Preventative Controls
definition: Preventative Controls deter and prevent cyber attacks and include infrastructure management, access management, device and end-point security, and secure coding.

name: Detective Controls
definition: Detective Controls include threat and vulnerability detection, anomalous activity detection, and event detection, may alert the institution to network and system irregularities that indicate an incident has or may occur.

name: Corrective Controls
definition: Corrective Controls are utilized to resolve system and software vulnerabilities through patch management and remediation of issues identified during vulnerability scans and penetration testing.

name: Connections
definition: Connections incorporate the identification, monitoring, and management of external connections and data flows to third parties.

name: Relationship Management
definition: Relationship Management includes due diligence, contracts, and ongoing monitoring to help ensure controls complement the institution’s cybersecurity program. May 2017 6 FFIEC Cybersecurity Assessment Tool User’s Guide

name: Incident Resilience Planning and Strategy
definition: Incident Resilience Planning & Strategy incorporates resilience planning and testing into existing business continuity and disaster recovery plans to minimize service disruptions and the destruction or corruption of data.

name: Detection, Response, and Mitigation
definition: Detection, Response, & Mitigation refers to the steps management takes to identify, prioritize, respond to, and mitigate the effects of internal and external threats and vulnerabilities.

name: Escalation and Reporting
definition: Escalation & Reporting ensures key stakeholders are informed about the impact of cyber incidents, and regulators, law enforcement, and customers are notified as required.
